instruction.text: Barbara is boiling one litre of water. After one minute, she reads the scale inside the pot. It reads 850 `ml`. Work out how much water has evaporated.
instruction.sound: Barbara is boiling one litre of water. After one minute, she reads the scale inside the pot. It reads 850 millilitres. Work out how much water has evaporated.

atoms.a: First, convert one litre into millilitres.
Next, subtract the reading after one minute from the initial amount.

instruction.text: One tree uses 100 `l` of water per day. Work out the volume of water 5 trees would use in 3 days.

atoms.a: First, work out how much water 5 trees use per day.
Next, multiply your answer by the number of days.

instruction.text: Lisa and Paul are preparing a juice for the school fair. They use 5000 `ml` of orange juice, 3700 `ml` of pineapple juice, 200 `ml` of raspberry juice, and 600 `ml` of apple juice. Work out the volume of juice in litres that they have they made in total.
instruction.sound: Lisa and Paul are preparing a juice for the school fair. They use 5000 ml of orange juice, 3700 ml of pineapple juice, 200 ml of raspberry juice, and 600 ml of apple juice. Work out the volume of juice in litres that they have made in total.

atoms.a: First, add up the quantities of orange juice and pineapple juice.
Next, add up the quantities of raspberry juice and apple juice.
Finally, convert your answer into litres.

instruction.text: Joe’s teapot has a capacity of 1.5 `l`, and one cup has a capacity of 300 `ml`. He says that he can pour six cups of tea from his teapot, is he correct?
instruction.sound: Joe’s teapot has a capacity of one and a half litres, and one cup has a capacity of 300 millilitres. He says that he can pour six cups of tea from his teapot, is he correct?

instruction.text: Work out how many cups of tea he can pour.

atoms.sound: First, convert one and a half litres into millilitres.

atoms.a: Next, divide the capacity of the teapot by the capacity of one cup.
